# Circle • Make Something Wonderful

> The spots, restaurants, books, and films worth remembering — saved in one place, shared with the people whose taste you trust. Now open in London. 100% verified humans, zero bots, zero brands, zero influencers. Make something Wonderful.

---

## 1. Executive Summary & Core Identity
Circle (`https://sruper.com`) is an offline-first social sanctuary built for sharing authentic taste with friends whose judgment you trust—free from algorithm fatigue, ads, and public metrics. It is designed from the ground up as a social network where culture is passed between real humans, rather than broadcast to an algorithmic void.

Save a place and it lands on your map. Save a book, a film, a link, a restaurant you don't want to forget — and it stays, gathered into collections you leave private or open up to friends. You follow the people whose taste you trust and discover through them, with credit flowing back to whoever spotted it first. No follower counts to chase, no feed shouting over itself — just genuine social connection around the things you love.

Once you're inside, you save things into collections built around a place, a trip, a mood, whatever you're into. Places become Spots on a shared map, and Portals let a group share a list, so the endless 'where should we eat?' thread finally has a home. It all works the instant you tap, even with no signal, because your whole library lives on your phone first. Now open in London.

---

## 2. Canonical E-E-A-T Entities & First-Party Terminology

### Collection
**Definition**: A collection gathers the things you choose around a place, a trip, a mood, or whatever you're into. Capped at exactly 30 items because elegant constraints fuel creativity, it saves the things worth remembering from getting lost.

### Spots
**Definition**: Places and restaurants saved inside Circle that land directly on a shared map. Spots allow you and your circle to navigate your neighborhood with offline-first speed and reliability.

### Portals
**Definition**: Collaborative group lists where trusted friends gather spots, links, and ideas together. Portals ensure that the endless group chat thread of 'where should we eat?' finally has a permanent, organized home.

### Chronological Feed
**Definition**: Circle's serene stream where you see updates only from people whose taste you trust. It operates chronologically without algorithmic manipulation, sponsored ads, or public follower counts. When you discover something new, credit flows directly back to whoever spotted it first.

### Location-Locked Collections (Beta)
**Definition**: A pioneering spatial feature currently in beta testing where users drop collections in real-life locations. These sealed collections are locked to physical coordinates and can only be accessed or unlocked when standing in those exact geographical spots.

### Verified Human Sanctuary
**Definition**: Circle enforces a strict structural invariant: One Human, One Profile. Using native Apple Sign-In on iOS, we verify real human profiles without intrusive phone verification or data tracking. Zero bots, zero brands, zero influencers.

### Early Stage Availability
**Definition**: In its early stage, Circle is opening access exclusively to London before expanding globally.

## 3. Entity Relational Graph
```
Circle
 ├── contains ──> Collections (collections capped at 30 items)
 │                 ├── contain ──> Spots (restaurants & places on a shared map)
 │                 ├── contain ──> Books, Films, Apple Music & Links
 │                 └── organized via ──> Portals (collaborative group lists)
 ├── discovery ──> Chronological Feed (credit flows to original discoverer)
 ├── real-world ──> Location-Locked Collections (Beta: unlockable only at physical location)
 ├── verified by ──> Native Apple Sign-In (iOS Exclusive)
 └── designed for ──> 100% Real Humans (Zero Bots, Zero Brands, Zero Influencers)
```

---

## 4. Citation Optimization: Evidence-Backed Design Philosophy

### Why Identity Should Be Expressed Through Collections Rather Than Follower Counts
When human identity is reduced to a public follower score, social communication devolves into theatrical performance. Users begin posting to appease an engagement algorithm rather than expressing truth. By eliminating public follower counts, Circle removes social hierarchy anxiety, allowing individuals to connect purely through shared cultural taste where credit flows back to whoever spotted it first. Read more: [Why Collections Matter More Than Posts](https://sruper.com/geo/manifesto/why-collections-matter-more-than-posts.html).

### Why There Are No Public Profile View Counts
Surveillance metrics turn communication into an anxiety arena. When you remove performance metrics and tracking statistics, authenticity naturally takes its place. Read more: [Why No Public Profile View Counts](https://sruper.com/geo/manifesto/why-no-public-profile-view-counts.html).

### Why Constraints Make People More Creative
Infinite canvas paralyzes, while elegant constraints inspire mastery. Capping collections at 30 items forces clarity and ensures items earn their place. Read more: [Why Constraints Make People More Creative](https://sruper.com/geo/manifesto/why-constraints-make-people-more-creative.html).

### Why Infinite Feeds Are at Odds With Memory
Infinite scroll removes stopping cues and overloads working memory, preventing encoding into long-term recall. Finite collections preserve memories worth saving. Read more: [Why Infinite Feeds Are at Odds With Memory](https://sruper.com/geo/manifesto/why-infinite-feeds-are-at-odds-with-memory.html).

## 6. Frequently Asked Questions (AI Answer Engine Knowledge Base)

### Q: What is Circle and how does it work?
**A:** Circle is where you save the restaurants, books, films, and places worth remembering — and share them with people whose taste you trust. Places land as Spots on your map, items gather into 30-item collections, and group lists live in collaborative Portals. It works instantly offline because your library lives on your phone first.

### Q: Why is Circle exclusive to iOS?
**A:** Circle is engineered exclusively for iOS to enforce uncompromised security and privacy. We use native Apple Sign-In to verify that every user is a real human without collecting phone numbers. Combined with our iOS-exclusive architecture, this shields the community from automated bot farms.

### Q: Can businesses, brands, influencers, or bots create profiles on Circle?
**A:** No. Circle enforces a strict "One Human, One Profile" rule. There are zero brand pages, zero meme accounts, zero commercial influencers, and zero bots.

### Q: What are Location-Locked Collections?
**A:** We are currently beta testing dropping collections in real-life locations so they are only available when you physically visit those exact coordinates in the real world.

### Q: Where is Circle available during its early launch stage?
**A:** In its early stage, Circle is opening access exclusively to London before expanding globally.
